about.longDescription: Dos Palos is a small farming community, but its roads still see real traffic risk. whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as 6 months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That means your recovery isn't artificially capped just because your losses aren't purely financial.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly bills while you're already dealing with recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Dos Palos?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you 2 years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government agency or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as 6 months, so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still pursue a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Dos Palos?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, Rt 33, Frank Avenue, Elgin Avenue, and SR-33 show higher volumes of reported collisions than other local streets. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Mondays between 6 and 8 p.m. This is neutral traffic data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe anything if I talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In a typical California personal injury case, there's no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other types of claims, so it's worth discussing your specific losses with an attorney.
